description.p: Status Hub gives the COSMIC panel a system tray. Applications that like to keep an icon near the clock — chat, music, sync, downloads, VPNs — gather behind a single hub button, and one click opens them together in a compact popup instead of spreading them across the panel.

The ones you reach for most can be pinned next to the hub, so they stay one click away. Every icon keeps the menu its own application provides, and you can drag them into the order you want, which is remembered from then on.

Status Hub is a tray of its own, written from the StatusNotifierItem specification rather than forked from COSMIC's Status Area, and built to run alongside it — so you can try it without giving anything up.

ul.li: One button in the panel instead of a row of icons
Pin what you use; everything else waits in the popup
An icon leaves with its application and comes back when it returns
One application that stops answering cannot hold up the panel or the other icons

description.p: Status Hub přináší do panelu COSMIC oznamovací oblast. Aplikace, které si rády nechávají ikonu u hodin — komunikátory, přehrávače, synchronizace, stahování, VPN — se shromáždí za jediným tlačítkem a jedno kliknutí je otevře pohromadě v úsporném vyskakovacím okně, místo aby se roztáhly po celém panelu.

Ty, po kterých saháte nejčastěji, si můžete připnout vedle tlačítka, takže zůstanou na jedno kliknutí. Každá ikona si ponechá nabídku, kterou nabízí její vlastní aplikace, a přetažením si je uspořádáte tak, jak chcete — pořadí si Status Hub zapamatuje.

Status Hub je samostatná oznamovací oblast, napsaná podle specifikace StatusNotifierItem, nikoli odvozená ze Stavové oblasti prostředí COSMIC, a je stavěná tak, aby běžela vedle ní — můžete ji tedy vyzkoušet, aniž byste se něčeho vzdali.

ul.li: Jedno tlačítko v panelu místo řady ikon
Připněte si, co používáte; zbytek počká ve vyskakovacím okně
Ikona zmizí spolu se svou aplikací a vrátí se, jakmile se vrátí i ona
Jedna aplikace, která přestane odpovídat, nemůže zdržet panel ani ostatní ikony

description.p: Status Hub gibt dem COSMIC-Panel einen Infobereich. Anwendungen, die gern ein Symbol neben der Uhr behalten – Chat, Musik, Synchronisierung, Downloads, VPNs – sammeln sich hinter einer einzigen Schaltfläche, und ein Klick öffnet sie gemeinsam in einem kompakten Fenster, statt sie über das Panel zu verteilen.

Die Symbole, die du am häufigsten brauchst, kannst du neben der Schaltfläche anheften; sie bleiben dann einen Klick entfernt. Jedes Symbol behält das Menü, das seine eigene Anwendung mitbringt, und per Ziehen bringst du sie in die Reihenfolge, die du willst – die wird von da an behalten.

Status Hub ist ein eigener Infobereich, geschrieben nach der StatusNotifierItem-Spezifikation statt aus COSMICs Statusbereich abgeleitet, und darauf ausgelegt, neben diesem zu laufen – du kannst es also ausprobieren, ohne etwas aufzugeben.

ul.li: Eine Schaltfläche im Panel statt einer Reihe von Symbolen
Hefte an, was du benutzt; alles andere wartet im Fenster
Ein Symbol geht mit seiner Anwendung und kommt zurück, wenn sie zurückkommt
Eine Anwendung, die nicht mehr antwortet, kann weder das Panel noch die anderen Symbole aufhalten

description.p: Status Hub le da al panel de COSMIC una bandeja del sistema. Las aplicaciones a las que les gusta dejar un icono junto al reloj — mensajería, música, sincronización, descargas, VPN — se reúnen detrás de un único botón, y con un clic se abren juntas en una ventana compacta en lugar de repartirse por el panel.

Los iconos que más usas se pueden fijar junto al botón, para que sigan a un clic de distancia. Cada icono conserva el menú que ofrece su propia aplicación, y puedes arrastrarlos hasta el orden que quieras, que se recuerda a partir de entonces.

Status Hub es una bandeja propia, escrita a partir de la especificación StatusNotifierItem en vez de derivada del Área de estado de COSMIC, y pensada para funcionar junto a ella: puedes probarla sin renunciar a nada.

ul.li: Un botón en el panel en lugar de una fila de iconos
Fija lo que uses; el resto espera en la ventana
Un icono se va con su aplicación y vuelve cuando ella vuelve
Una aplicación que deja de responder no puede frenar el panel ni los demás iconos

description.p: Status Hub donne au panneau COSMIC une zone de notification. Les applications qui aiment garder une icône près de l’horloge — messagerie, musique, synchronisation, téléchargements, VPN — se regroupent derrière un seul bouton, et un clic les ouvre ensemble dans une fenêtre compacte au lieu de les étaler sur le panneau.

Celles dont vous vous servez le plus peuvent être épinglées à côté du bouton, pour rester à un clic. Chaque icône conserve le menu fourni par sa propre application, et vous pouvez les faire glisser dans l’ordre que vous voulez : il est retenu ensuite.

Status Hub est une zone de notification à part entière, écrite d’après la spécification StatusNotifierItem plutôt que dérivée de la Zone d’état de COSMIC, et conçue pour fonctionner à côté d’elle — vous pouvez donc l’essayer sans rien abandonner.

ul.li: Un bouton dans le panneau au lieu d’une rangée d’icônes
Épinglez ce que vous utilisez ; le reste attend dans la fenêtre
Une icône part avec son application et revient quand celle-ci revient
Une application qui cesse de répondre ne peut bloquer ni le panneau ni les autres icônes

description.p: Status Hub dà al pannello di COSMIC un’area di notifica. Le applicazioni a cui piace tenere un’icona vicino all’orologio — chat, musica, sincronizzazione, download, VPN — si raccolgono dietro un solo pulsante, e un clic le apre tutte insieme in una finestra compatta invece di spargerle per il pannello.

Quelle che usi di più puoi fissarle accanto al pulsante, così restano a un clic di distanza. Ogni icona mantiene il menu fornito dalla sua applicazione, e puoi trascinarle nell’ordine che preferisci: da quel momento viene ricordato.

Status Hub è un’area di notifica a sé, scritta partendo dalla specifica StatusNotifierItem anziché derivata dall’Area di stato di COSMIC, e pensata per funzionare accanto a essa: puoi provarla senza rinunciare a nulla.

ul.li: Un pulsante nel pannello invece di una fila di icone
Fissa quelle che usi; tutte le altre aspettano nella finestra
Un’icona se ne va con la sua applicazione e torna quando torna lei
Un’applicazione che smette di rispondere non può bloccare il pannello né le altre icone

description.p: Status Hub geeft het COSMIC-paneel een systeemvak. Toepassingen die graag een pictogram bij de klok houden — chat, muziek, synchronisatie, downloads, VPN’s — verzamelen zich achter één knop, en met één klik gaan ze samen open in een compact venster in plaats van verspreid over het paneel.

De pictogrammen die je het vaakst nodig hebt, kun je naast de knop vastzetten, zodat ze op één klik afstand blijven. Elk pictogram houdt het menu dat zijn eigen toepassing meelevert, en je kunt ze in de volgorde slepen die jij wilt; die wordt daarna onthouden.

Status Hub is een systeemvak op zichzelf, geschreven vanuit de StatusNotifierItem-specificatie in plaats van afgeleid van COSMIC’s statusgebied, en gemaakt om er naast te draaien — je kunt het dus uitproberen zonder iets op te geven.

ul.li: Eén knop in het paneel in plaats van een rij pictogrammen
Zet vast wat je gebruikt; de rest wacht in het venster
Een pictogram vertrekt met zijn toepassing en komt terug wanneer die terugkomt
Eén toepassing die niet meer antwoordt kan het paneel of de andere pictogrammen niet ophouden

description.p: Status Hub daje panelowi COSMIC obszar powiadomień. Programy, które lubią trzymać ikonę przy zegarze — komunikatory, odtwarzacze, synchronizacja, pobieranie, VPN — zbierają się za jednym przyciskiem, a jedno kliknięcie otwiera je razem w zwartym okienku, zamiast rozciągać po całym panelu.

Te, po które sięgasz najczęściej, możesz przypiąć obok przycisku, żeby zostały o jedno kliknięcie. Każda ikona zachowuje menu, które daje jej własny program, a przeciąganiem ustawisz je w wybranej kolejności — od tej pory zostanie zapamiętana.

Status Hub to osobny obszar powiadomień, napisany według specyfikacji StatusNotifierItem, a nie odgałęziony od Obszaru stanu COSMIC, i przygotowany tak, by działać obok niego — możesz go więc wypróbować, niczego nie tracąc.

ul.li: Jeden przycisk w panelu zamiast rzędu ikon
Przypnij to, czego używasz; reszta poczeka w okienku
Ikona znika razem ze swoim programem i wraca, gdy on wraca
Jeden program, który przestaje odpowiadać, nie zatrzyma panelu ani pozostałych ikon

description.p: O Status Hub dá ao painel do COSMIC uma bandeja do sistema. Os aplicativos que gostam de deixar um ícone perto do relógio — mensageiros, players, sincronização, downloads, VPNs — se reúnem atrás de um único botão, e um clique abre todos juntos numa janelinha compacta, em vez de espalhá-los pelo painel.

Os que você mais usa podem ser fixados ao lado do botão, para continuarem a um clique de distância. Cada ícone mantém o menu que o próprio aplicativo oferece, e você pode arrastá-los para a ordem que quiser — dali em diante ela fica guardada.

O Status Hub é uma bandeja própria, escrita a partir da especificação StatusNotifierItem e não derivada da Área de status do COSMIC, feita para rodar ao lado dela — dá para experimentar sem abrir mão de nada.

ul.li: Um botão no painel em vez de uma fileira de ícones
Fixe o que você usa; o resto espera na janelinha
O ícone vai embora junto com o aplicativo e volta quando ele volta
Um aplicativo que para de responder não trava o painel nem os outros ícones

description.p: Status Hub добавляет панели COSMIC системный лоток. Приложения, которые любят держать значок у часов — мессенджеры, плееры, синхронизация, загрузки, VPN, — собираются за одной кнопкой, и один щелчок открывает их все вместе в компактном окне, вместо того чтобы растягивать по всей панели.

Те, к которым вы обращаетесь чаще всего, можно закрепить рядом с кнопкой, и они останутся в одном щелчке. Каждый значок сохраняет меню, которое даёт его собственное приложение, а перетаскиванием вы расставите их в нужном порядке — дальше он запоминается.

Status Hub — самостоятельный лоток, написанный по спецификации StatusNotifierItem, а не ответвлённый от области состояния COSMIC, и рассчитанный на работу рядом с ней: попробовать можно, ничем не жертвуя.

ul.li: Одна кнопка на панели вместо ряда значков
Закрепите то, чем пользуетесь; остальное подождёт в окне
Значок уходит вместе со своим приложением и возвращается вместе с ним
Одно переставшее отвечать приложение не задержит ни панель, ни остальные значки

description.p: Status Hub додає панелі COSMIC системний лоток. Програми, які люблять тримати піктограму біля годинника — месенджери, програвачі, синхронізація, завантаження, VPN, — збираються за однією кнопкою, і одне клацання відкриває їх разом у компактному віконці, замість розтягувати по всій панелі.

Ті, до яких ви звертаєтеся найчастіше, можна закріпити поруч із кнопкою, і вони лишаться за одне клацання. Кожна піктограма зберігає меню, яке дає її власна програма, а перетягуванням ви розставите їх у потрібному порядку — далі він запам’ятовується.
Status Hub — самостійний лоток, написаний за специфікацією StatusNotifierItem, а не відгалужений від області стану COSMIC, і розрахований на роботу поруч із нею: спробувати можна, нічим не жертвуючи.

ul.li: Одна кнопка на панелі замість ряду піктограм
Закріпіть те, чим користуєтеся; решта зачекає у віконці
Піктограма зникає разом зі своєю програмою і повертається разом із нею
Одна програма, що перестала відповідати, не затримає ні панель, ні інші піктограми

description.p: Status Hub 为 COSMIC 面板带来系统托盘。那些喜欢在时钟旁留一个图标的应用——聊天、音乐、同步、下载、VPN——统统收进一个按钮后面，点一下就在紧凑的弹窗里一起打开，而不是散落在整条面板上。
最常用的那几个可以固定在按钮旁边，始终只差一次点击。每个图标都保留其应用自带的菜单，你还可以拖动排出想要的顺序，此后一直记住。
Status Hub 是一套独立的托盘，依据 StatusNotifierItem 规范编写，而非从 COSMIC 的状态区域分支而来，并且刻意做成可以与它并存——你尽可放心试用，不必舍弃什么。

ul.li: 面板上只有一个按钮，而不是一排图标
常用的固定出来，其余的留在弹窗里等着
应用退出时图标随之消失，应用回来时图标也回来
某个应用不再响应，也拖不住面板和其他图标

description.p: This release lets you put the hub's own button on whichever side of the pinned items you prefer, and stops an application's help text standing in for its name.

ul.li: Adds a Button position setting to the Appearance section: the hub's button sits at the left or the right of the pinned items, whichever you choose, and stays there. It replaces a rule that read the panel's own configuration to work out which end faced away from the screen centre — a guess that had no answer at all for a centred panel and no way for you to overrule it. On a vertical panel the two choices are the top and the bottom.
Starts the button on the right. If the panel had been placing it on the left for you, choose Left once in settings and it stays.

Names a tray item by the first line of the title its application publishes. IBus puts its name and a sentence about middle-clicking the panel icon in that one field, which arrived as a single run-on label; now only the name shows. Any application with the same habit is covered.

description.p: This patch finds icons the icon theme in use does not carry, reaches those snap packages publish, and gives the Save button the hover it was missing.

ul.li: Looks an application's icon up in every icon theme installed on the system before falling back to guessing from the item's name, so an application whose artwork only ships in a theme you are not currently wearing keeps its own icon instead of a generic one. The themes COSMIC ships come first and the rest follow by name, so two machines resolve the same application to the same artwork.
Reads the icons snap packages publish, through read-only access to the three trees snapd uses.

Gives the Save button in settings the hover and press shading the settings button it replaces has, and holds it to the same box. Its padding no longer follows the interface density, which at the spacious setting had been pushing the label out of the header.

description.p: This patch quiets the system log and finishes the popup header's buttons.

ul.li: Leaves the system log alone during ordinary use. Every icon lookup, click and menu change was written to the journal, which buried anything else being debugged there; the tray's own comings and goings are still reported, and the rest is available on request.
Marks the Save button in settings with a check beside its label, so it matches the buttons that do the same job elsewhere in COSMIC.

description.p: This patch lines up the settings entry that appears when no app is in the tray.

ul.li: Marks the "No apps available" line in settings with a glyph of its own, so it lines up with every other row in the list instead of starting flush against the edge.

description.p: This patch settles the popup header on the desktop's own icon and the theme's ordinary ink.

ul.li: Draws the settings button with the desktop's own icon, so it matches every other applet whatever icon theme is installed, in place of the glyph compiled into the binary.
Paints the settings and save buttons in the theme's ordinary text colour, rather than picking the settings icon out in the accent colour.
Marks the repository link with the same glyph the developer's other applets use.

description.p: This patch gives the settings popup its own icons and a Links section.

ul.li: Adds a Links section to settings, opening the issue tracker, the repository, and the developer's page in the browser.
Ships the popup's icons compiled into the binary, so the settings button, section headings, and drag handles look the same whatever icon theme is installed.
Heads each settings section with an icon and gives every row its own icon.
Sizes a settings row to the text it holds, shortening an over-long label instead of reserving two lines on every row.

description.p: This patch adds Czech to the languages Status Hub speaks.

ul.li: Adds the Czech applet translation and localizes the desktop entry and AppStream metadata in Czech.
Keeps the Czech catalogue covered by the translation parity test.

description.p: This patch improves icon recovery and theme loading while completing translated application metadata.

ul.li: Falls back to a tray item's application identifier when its published icon is missing or invalid, before using the generic icon.
Lets the Flatpak create COSMIC's versioned configuration directories so it reliably loads the host theme.
Adds the Polish applet translation and localizes the desktop entry and AppStream metadata in every supported language.
Keeps the Polish catalogue covered by the translation parity test.

description.p: This maintenance release keeps Status Hub aligned with COSMIC Epoch 1.8 and the latest libcosmic APIs.

ul.li: Updates libcosmic, COSMIC panel configuration and their Rust dependency graph.
Refreshes the vendored Flatpak sources so offline builds use the same dependency revisions.
Updates the GitHub Actions checkout integration used by continuous integration and releases.

description.p: Tray icons now retain their detail more reliably across themes and panel sizes.

ul.li: Recolours only symbolic, neutral monotone and simple neutral duotone artwork, leaving coloured icons and complex outlines unchanged.
Recognizes antialiased simple artwork without mistaking broad gradients or layered contours for a themeable icon.
Preserves embedded notification badges and composes published overlay icons independently in every applet view.
Rasterizes and resizes all supported icon sources independently of recolouring, using high-resolution rendering and premultiplied-alpha filtering.
Selects better SNI pixmap frames and keeps non-square artwork proportional.

description.p: The settings popup no longer scrolls while its content still fits, and the panel icon and the grid of tray icons have been redrawn around their own weight.

ul.li: Stops the settings popup scrolling from the first item on. The appearance row came from a settings item whose spacer left the label a third of the row, wrapping it over three lines the layout had never budgeted for.
Sizes the settings list from the content it holds, up to the popup's ceiling, instead of a height worked out in advance, so a row that measures differently can no longer clip the list.
Holds the horizontal inset of the settings rows at a single value whatever the density does, and gives the row dragged across the list the same inset as the rows it moves between.
Lines a wrapped setting's second line up with its first, which had kept the space it wrapped on and sat a character further right.
Redraws the panel icon on three heavier dots and drops the outline around them, so it stays separate and legible at the size the panel paints it.
Centres the tray icons in the popup as one block, while each row still fills from the start.

description.p: The installed executable now follows the COSMIC external applet naming convention.

ul.li: Renames the applet and diagnostic binaries to the cosmic-ext-applet-status-hub namespace.
Updates native and Flatpak launch metadata to use the renamed executable consistently.

description.p: Status Hub now has its own panel icon and cooperates with the panel when space is limited.

ul.li: Replaces the generic overflow glyph with a dedicated symbolic Status Hub icon.
Marks the applet as shrinkable so the panel can move it into overflow when necessary.
Installs the symbolic icon in native and Flatpak packages so it resolves consistently after installation.

description.p: The popup and the settings view now follow the desktop theme instead of a single density baked into the code, and the settings list is built from the same components COSMIC uses elsewhere.

ul.li: Sizes the settings list, its rows and its section titles from the theme's own spacing, so a compact or spacious desktop no longer leaves dead space at the foot of the popup or scrolls before the list is full.
Keeps the popup's outer margin at one comfortable value whatever the density, so content never crowds the edge, and lines the header separator up with the title above it.
Rebuilds the settings rows on the list components from libcosmic, which gives them hover feedback, rounded ends and the theme's own highlight while a row is dragged.
Centres the settings button in the header, which drifted sideways on any density other than the default.
Hides the scrollbars, which also returns the strip of width they reserved over the right edge of the content.
Raises the ceiling on the settings popup so more of the tray is visible before it scrolls.
Stops resolving and repainting the overlay icon that was never drawn, and keeps icon lookup behind its cache, so opening the popup does less work per frame.

description.p: Icons can now keep the colours their application published, and the ones Status Hub does repaint come out closer to the artwork they were made from.

ul.li: Adds an appearance setting that decides whether tray icons follow the panel theme or keep their published colours. Explicit symbolic icons and generic fallbacks still follow the panel, so nothing turns illegible when the setting is off.
Paints detailed vector icons through the same analysis as bitmaps, instead of the approximation a colour matrix in the file allowed, so an SVG and a PNG of the same artwork now come out alike.
Reads the usable tone range from the body of an icon alone, so a single highlight or a dark outline no longer flattens everything else.
Keeps a badge's outline out of that measurement and blends the badge itself with a fifth of the panel ink, so the accent survives while the badge still reads as part of the icon.
Groups the settings view into an appearance section and a tray section, and scrolls the list instead of growing a popup taller than the screen when many applications are in the tray.

description.p: Tray icons keep their detail on both light and dark panels, and the settings list finally names applications correctly.

ul.li: Repaints every icon so its shading always moves away from the panel behind it, within a fixed budget. Dark detail no longer sinks into a dark panel and light detail no longer washes out on a light one, while a coloured badge keeps the colours the application drew it with.
Reorders the tray by dragging items in the settings list, and remembers that order across restarts.
Pins as many items as you like. The panel still shows only what fits its monitor and keeps the rest in the popup, so the previous limit of sixteen only refused pins you could reach anyway.
Names an application by its title rather than its tooltip, which many use for status text: the list showed "you have 1 notification" for Slack and the transfer speeds for qBittorrent.
Tells apart trays that publish the same generic Chromium identifier, so 1Password and Chrome no longer compete for the same pin.
Stops asking again for a property an application has already refused, instead of retrying it for a minute.

description.p: Clicking a tray item now brings the application's window forward, even when the application has no way to do that itself.

ul.li: Raises the window for applications that do not implement ProvideXdgActivationToken, every Chromium and Electron tray among them, which under Wayland can neither take focus nor restore a minimized window. Applications that do implement it are handed the token and left to decide, so a menu entry meant only to start a recording no longer disturbs the window.
Rounds the hover of the first and last menu entry to follow the popup's corner radius, instead of overflowing it.
Dims menu entries the application marked unavailable, which were drawn in the same colour as the ones that can be clicked.

description.p: No user-visible change. Corrects a test that assumed a COSMIC icon theme is installed, which made the suite fail on a machine without one.
Icons an application publishes from inside its own sandbox now resolve, tray artwork is adapted to the panel it sits on, and the Flatpak asks for far fewer permissions.

ul.li: Finds an icon whose directory means something only inside the publishing application's own sandbox, by looking for the same artwork in that application's Flatpak payload. Dropbox and Steam show the icons they ship instead of a generic one, and the rule carries no per-application knowledge, so any application publishing such a path is covered.

Adapts achromatic tray artwork to the panel, so a glyph drawn for a dark panel no longer disappears on a light one. Artwork that already reads is left untouched, judged by how much of its ink contrasts with the panel and whether that ink traces the whole shape, rather than by an average tone that no part of the artwork actually has.

Asks for eleven permissions instead of fifteen. Read access to every Flatpak application's private data, to the host system tree and to the user's icon directory is gone, since Flatpak already exposes the host icon themes on its own; both export grants are narrowed to their icons subtree.

description.p: Items can be pinned to the panel, the popup gained a settings view, and the interface is available in ten languages.

ul.li: Pin any tray item to the panel, where it sits beside the hub button and stays one click away. Pins are remembered between sessions, survive an application restarting under a new bus name, and are kept in step across every panel.

Adds a header to the popup, with a settings view behind it listing every item and a switch for pinning it. Choices are applied when they are saved and discarded if the popup is dismissed, so the panel never shifts while they are being made.
Replaces the panel chevron with a button that no longer changes with the popup state, and keeps it at the end of the applet that faces away from the screen, so pinning an item does not move it.
Keeps a popup item's menu in the same card behind a divider, while a menu opened from a pinned item is anchored to that item's own panel slot.
Prefers the icon theme over the icon file an application ships alongside itself, so the tray follows the theme where one is available.
Shows the panel button even when the tray is empty, so the settings view can always be reached, and centres an explanatory notice in the popup.
Translated interface in English, Brazilian Portuguese, Dutch, French, German, Italian, Russian, Simplified Chinese, Spanish, and Ukrainian.

description.p: Left click brings the application to the front again, and the tray follows the usual mouse controls.

ul.li: Asks the panel for its privileged Wayland connection, which is what lets the compositor grant a real activation token. Without it the token was issued but only marked the window urgent, so an application such as ZapZap was told to activate and never came to the front.

Restores the standard tray controls: left click activates the application, middle click requests its optional secondary action, and right click opens its menu. Left click no longer falls back to the menu when activation fails, and no longer defers to the menu for items that advertise one.

Finds an icon the application publishes under its own IconThemePath before consulting the icon theme, and only accepts a result that really lives there, so an icon theme carrying a same-named copy can no longer win.
Retries an icon that fell back to the generic one, on a schedule stretching to about a minute, for applications that publish their icon shortly after registering.
Coalesces menu layout requests and discards a layout older than the one already shown, so an application redrawing its menu repeatedly cannot flicker or go backwards.
Stops a slow menu announcement from delaying the first layout, so a menu opens as soon as its contents are known.
Widens the popup only when a menu is on screen, leaving the tray at the width its icons need.
Collapses the panel button to nothing while there are no tray items, instead of holding an empty gap.

description.p: Icons published by Flatpak applications are found again.

ul.li: Reads the Flatpak installation directories, so the icons exported by a Flatpak application resolve. They are symbolic links into those directories, and without them every such icon fell back to the generic one whenever the active icon theme did not happen to carry a copy.
Reads the per-application Flatpak data directories, where an application such as Steam keeps the icon it names in IconThemePath. Read only, and only what those applications publish.
Looks an icon name up once, letting the path the item published win over the icon theme.
Ignores an empty icon theme path instead of searching it as a relative directory.
Reports the file each icon resolved to, so a missing icon can be diagnosed from the log.
Reads the COSMIC configuration without asking to write it.
Asks again when an application answers only part of its properties. A slow application could leave an item with no menu, and therefore no right click, until it was restarted.
Keeps retrying for about two minutes rather than twelve seconds, which is closer to how long a busy application takes to answer.

description.p: First release.

ul.li: Collects StatusNotifierItem tray items behind a single panel button.
Renders DBusMenu menus, including submenus, checkmarks, and radio groups.
Removes items when their bus owner disappears, so no icon is left stranded.
Applies a timeout and a per-item error budget to every remote call.
Keeps a stable item order that does not depend on reply timing.
Runs alongside COSMIC's own Status Area.
